abstract: This paper describes several control strategies to utilise a modern battery energy storage system (BESS) to provide simultaneous control of both its MW and MVAr outputs to improve power system operation and control with the following objective in mind: ability to absorb harmonics, provide load leveling, provide damping of inter-area oscillations, help in damping transient stability, provide effective and fast control power flow along a transmission line corridor, in many ways acting like flexible AC transmission system (FACTS) devices, provide back-up electricity supply on loss of AC supply very similar to UPS applications and provide active power filtering to meet power quality standards. This work shows that BESS offers an important resource for improving power system control.

articleTitle: Free moving metallic particle detection in GIS
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: High reliability of gas insulated switchgear apparatus is diminished by the presence of defects inside the system. The most common defects are due to metallic particles. This defect can be detected by several techniques, one of which is that using acoustic sensors placed on the enclosure. This paper presents the technique to detect metallic particle from the parameters of acoustic signal such as maximum acoustic amplitude and number of pulses which exceed the specified level of maximum acoustic amplitude at different supply voltage.

articleTitle: Neural network application in directional comparison carrier protection of EHV transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: The increasing scale and complexity of power systems require high performance and high reliability of power system protection. Protective relaying based on directional comparison with power line carrier or microwave channels is the most suitable protection scheme for long distance EHV transmission lines and widely used in power systems. The key element of such protection is the directional relay used to discriminate fault direction. In order to overcome the disadvantages of conventional directional relays, the authors of this paper put forward a directional comparison carrier protection scheme based on artificial neural networks (ANNs). The protection is extensively tested using the electromagnetic transient program (EMTP) under various electric power system operating and fault conditions. It is proved that the directional comparison carrier protection based on ANNs, which can recognize various fault patterns of the protected transmission line (such as fault direction, fault phases, etc.) correctly under any kind of operating and fault conditions and the whole process, is satisfactory for EHV transmission line protection.

articleTitle: Dynamic simulation of the nuclear power plant auxiliaries
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: The scale and complexity of present day power systems are increasing. To plan and design such a system, it is necessary to have computer models for both the transmission grid and the power plant in detail. As an example of computer simulation support for designers, this paper presents the upgrading procedure of 6 kV bus transfer system in a large nuclear power plant. There are described some important features of the NPP electrical diagram and issues connected with bus transfer and its simulation. The paper outlines a general purpose automaton model used for relays and protection systems simulation. Several examples of transient phenomena computation illustrate using the advanced network simulator MODES for power system analysis and protection design.

articleTitle: Short-term load forecasting using recurrent neutral networks
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: This paper has proposed the prediction of hourly load in power systems through two recurrent neutral networks, one based on multilayer perception models with a second order learning rule and the second on radial basis function network. Two different formulations of load forecasting have been simulated, one to predict hourly load based on historical data and the second to predict peak and valley loads of a particular day type and then forecasting the hourly load using a normalized load curve of that day type. The results obtained on a practical Indian system data demonstrate that the second approach based on prediction of peak and valley load for a day type along with radial basis function network model provides more accurate forecast of the load.

articleTitle: Longer-term voltage stability calculation by simulated annealing algorithm
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: An improved algorithm for global nonlinear optimization is presented. The scheme is based on combination of the nonlinear simplex with a simulated annealing (SA) algorithm. This improved algorithm is shown to provide faster execution time without compromising the quality of solutions obtained. The nonlinear simplex algorithm is adopted to decrease the amount of calculation. The results obtained reveal the adequacy of the algorithm for the global optimization of problems. Then the improved algorithm is adopted to calculate the longer-term voltage stability limit. Both nonlinear equality and inequality constraints for the longer-term voltage stability limit are considered. A sample system with a five-bus power system shows that the developed algorithm is effective and valid.

articleTitle: Adaptive pole-placement controller for HVDC link
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: This paper describes the design of a self-tuning feedback controller based on the pole-placement algorithm. The controller is designed for a composite AC-DC system and aims to improve the transient performance of the AC system during disturbances. Results are obtained from computer simulation runs using a software package known as PSASP.

articleTitle: Modelling strategy for isolated power systems employing synchronous motor drives
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: This paper details a modelling strategy for isolated power systems employing synchronous motor drives. The model detailed has two functions: to predict transient performance and waveform distortion. A transient simulation showing a system's response to a change in motor speed demand is detailed and the extent of waveform distortion in isolated power systems is considered.

articleTitle: Energy transaction scheduling with network constraints and transmission losses
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach to study the energy transaction scheduling for market-based operation using network flow programming (NFP). The proposed model includes network constraints and transmission losses. In the old paradigm, most of the schedules considered bilateral contracts. Research work showed that a multilateral contract is needed for efficient market operation. In this study, the proposed method is based on the premise that there are no firm contracts in the energy transaction system. Every contract in the energy transaction system is considered as a multilateral contract. An independent system operator (ISO) is assumed to be the broker. The broker maximises the number of transactions subject to power flow equations, buying and selling contracts and network constraints. This leads to a problem of network flow programming (NFP) with upper and lower limits. So a special solution in NFP "out-of-kilter algorithm" (OKA) is employed. A test example of IEEE 30 bus system is presented for the proposed model and method.

articleTitle: A new approach to analysis of inter-turns faults of three-phase induction motors
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: In order to improve the internal-fault simulation of three-phase induction motors, the authors present the basic idea of the "bidirectional revolving magnetic fields" concept, i.e. each coil carrying AC current will produce a pulsating MMF that can be decomposed into two opposite-directional revolving MMFs. One can then synthesize the effects of all coil MMFs according to actual inner-faults in order to take the place of the symmetrical components method in solving the internal faults of induction motors. In addition, the motor parameters are influenced by internal faults, for example, the slot leakage reactances, even if referred to the same number of turns, are still unequal, and the same is true of the resistances, which have been considered in this paper. On the basis of these ideas, a new mathematical model and a corresponding computation program have been built, and simulation results have also been obtained. The simulation results are quite approximate to the measured data. This analysis method is accurate enough and simpler than other methods, such as the multi-loop method.

articleTitle: Effective loadflow technique with non-constant MVA load for the Hong Kong Mass Transit Railway urban lines power distribution system
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: The power distribution systems of Hong Kong's Mass Transit Railway Corporation consist of loads having different voltage dependent characteristics. However, conventional load flow methods are not adequate for accurate power system studies and for fast contingency studies. A load modelling technique, in which each voltage dependent load is modelled by a Norton equivalent comprising of a 2/spl times/2 admittance matrix and a current vector, is introduced in this paper. Because this load model is always tangential to the actual load characteristics, a primitive nodal method can be employed. The proposed technique is easily programmed and converges rapidly. The advantages of the proposed technique are further discussed with respect to conventional load flow methods with constant MVA loads.

articleTitle: Advanced economic dispatching control algorithm using dynamic unit model and interior point method
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: Economic dispatching control (EDC) is one of the most important functions of a central load dispatching center of power utilities. The conventional EDC algorithm that employs the equal incremental fuel cost method minimizes the fuel costs subject to the system energy balance. It is, however, unable to treat power unit dynamics and generator constraints that extend over plural time slices. In this paper, we propose a new economic dispatching control algorithm that takes unit dynamics into consideration to lower fuel costs and is able to treat various kinds of constraints using the interior point optimization method.

articleTitle: Modelling static phase shifters in multi-machine power systems
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: Static phase shifters (SPSs) are new FACTS devices. They can offer both static and dynamic controls of power flows in power systems. This paper reports the build-up of an SPS mathematical model that can be applied to the transient stability analysis of a multimachine system. The simulation results reveal the potential of using SPS for enhancing the transient stability of power systems.

articleTitle: Visualization and interactive simulation for power system operation and education
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: Interactive simulation by software is becoming widely used as computers are improved in speed. A lot of efforts to visualize simulation results are reported. Though simulation and visualization are needed in every field in power system management, required functions in simulation and effective visualizations depend upon the purpose of them in each field. We study interaction in power system simulation. Interaction is required in creating power system models and changing electric parameters. We also examine the visualization which is effective in power utilities. Combinations of topological display and graphical representations are effective for humans to understand power system behavior. We developed a power system education system which realizes the interactive simulation and relevant visualization. The system is used in education courses and an operational planning department in a utility.

articleTitle: Incorporating generator reactive power limits into constrained-genetic-algorithm load flow
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: This paper develops a method to deal with the generator reactive power limits in a genetic algorithm-based environment. In this method, the limits are treated as inequality constraints. The developed method for treating the reactive power limits and the technique usually adopted in Newton-Raphson load flow are compared. The validity and performance of the constrained-genetic-algorithm load flow with generator reactive power limit treatment are tested and illustrated by applying the method to the IEEE 30-bus test system.

articleTitle: Short-term load forecasting using fuzzy neural network
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: In this paper, a new model of fuzzy neural network (FNN) is presented for power system short-term load forecasting. This model can deal with the uncertain elements more efficiently. This paper also presents an artificial neural network (ANN) based defuzzification method. Using this method one can easily process defuzzification without regard to the complication of the fuzzification algorithm and get high accuracy of defuzzification.

articleTitle: A QFT based robust SVC controller for improving the dynamic stability of power systems
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: A novel design technique for an SVC-based power system damping controller has been proposed. The controller attempts to place all plant poles within a specified region on the s-plane to guarantee the desired close loop performance. The use of Horowitz's quantitative feedback theory (QFT) permits the design of a "fixed gain controller" which maintains its performance in spite of large variations in the plant parameters during its normal course of operation. The performance of this robust controller has been evaluated on a single machine infinite bus system equipped with a mid point SVC and the results are shown to be consistent with the expected performance of the stabilizer.

articleTitle: The effects of fault clearance practices on adjustable speed drives
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: Rapid three-phase "fuse saving" fault clearance practice has been widely used in power systems. However, most of the faults on power systems are single-line-to-ground (SLG) faults. Under this condition, single-phase tripping with automatic reclosure can be an attractive alternative because it only introduces short term disruption of power supply to the faulted phase. It has not been widely used in distribution systems because of the consideration that it could lead to some imbalance to three-phase loads such as adjustable speed drives (ASD). The study compares the effects of three-phase tripping with that of single-phase tripping on ASD. It is shown that single-phase tripping improves the quality of power supply. Also, the degree of imbalance during fault clearance is considered acceptable.

articleTitle: Losses reduction in power distribution by means of switching factors method
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: Feeder reconfiguration is defined as altering the topology of a distribution network by transferring loads from a heavily loaded feeder section to a more lightly loaded feeder section to minimize the losses. In this paper a new method of loss reduction is proposed. This method is very reliable and accurate compared to the existing methods. It can also be used to calculate the price of kWh for customer's service in case of budgetary reason.

articleTitle: Decentralized H/sup /spl infin// control for stabilizing multi-machine power systems
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: This paper applies the decentralized H/sup /spl infin// control theory to interconnected multi-machine power systems. The idea is to design a local controller for each machine model with global sub-optimal H/sup /spl infin// control performance with considering the interactions among multi-machine systems. The sub-optimal H/sup /spl infin// state feedback controller for each machine is calculated by the algorithm based on the linear matrix inequality (LMI). The control input for each machine is implemented by supplementary excitation control. The disturbance to each subsystem is modeled by perturbation of the terminal voltage, which is raised by the simultaneous reactance change of the transmission line. The proposed control design scheme is applied to a three-machine loop system and a three machine radial system. The frequency responses and transient responses for each machine and the global system are evaluated by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: The effect of integration of wind farms into utility network on voltage control due to the co-ordination of AVC relays
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of wind generation systems, i.e. wind farms, on the voltage control of the public distribution system. A previous study has shown that voltage magnitude of a distribution system can be controlled successfully in the absence of embedded generators by using on-load tap-changer transformer(s). However the integration of wind farms into distribution systems has resulted in unacceptable voltage fluctuation. This paper highlights the impact of the frequent variation of wind farms output and the co-ordination of AVC relays at different voltage levels on system power quality. The responses of AVC relays due to wind power fluctuation and different tap operation sequences are analysed.

articleTitle: Intelligent system applications in a competitive power industry environment
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: The emerging competitive power industry environment is creating new engineering and economic problems whose solution may best be achieved with the help of intelligent systems. In this environment of open access to the power transmission systems, the economics and reliability associated with differing power producers needs to be evaluated. An increase in the number of electric energy transactions accompanies the creation of new players in the competitive environment. Evaluation and management of electric energy contracts requires real-time decision support tools. Independent System Operators are emerging as the entity responsible for operation and control of the transmission network. As a result of the need to maximize profits while controlling the costs and maintaining system reliability, new intelligent system applications are needed to meet the new challenges of economics, reliability and power quality. Evaluating transactions requires the automation of intelligent verification of contract feasibility from an economic and reliability point-of-view. To manage the planning process, newly available data needs to be intelligently processed. For example, this data includes measurements needed to support power quality assessment. These intelligent systems can be integrated with information systems that are capable of handling large volumes of data.

articleTitle: Advanced arresters for GIS with new zinc-oxide elements
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: New zinc-oxide elements with a varistor voltage about twice that of conventional ones of the same thickness have been developed by reducing the ZnO grain size with a new additive, which enable to halve the series number of elements in metal oxide surge arresters. The advanced arresters with these elements for GIS are compact by 40 to 60% in volume compared with conventional ones. The electrical and mechanical performance of the advanced arresters was satisfactory through the various evaluation tests such as thermal stability test, residual voltage test, seismic test, long-term stability test etc.

articleTitle: Study on DC power modulation in AC/DC power system
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: The influence of DC power modulation on transient stability for an interconnected AC/DC power system is studied and some regularity conclusions are made in this paper. The engineering feasibility and existing problems of improving the transient stability by fast DC power modulation is also studied when the AC system is subjected to a large disturbance. Moreover, it is discussed whether DC power modulation absorbs a large amount of reactive power, and possibly leads to voltage collapse of the AC system. The simulation results prove that the effectiveness of DC power modulation to improve the transient stability of an interconnected AC/DC power system is subject to the network structure of the system, the parameters and reactive power characteristics in the AC system, the types of modulator, their parameters and the operation mode in the DC system.

articleTitle: Towards the development of PC-based intelligent alarm processor in China Light and Power Company
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: This paper describes the initial experiences of CLP in the development of an intelligent alarm processor integrating with the existing real-time energy management system (EMS). The system adopts a commercially available knowledge-based software package which runs on a personal computer platform. Ease of implementation, minimum interference to real-time system and low cost are the characteristics of the system. Special consideration has been given to minimizing the maintenance burden on the power system topology. The system adopts a hypothesis-based approach in modeling the dispatcher's interpretation process during power system disturbance. Initial testing of the system produces satisfactory results. The system will be put into real-time operation after some further enhancements.

articleTitle: New load flow technique based on load transfer and load buses elimination
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: A new load flow methodology based on load transfer and load buses elimination is proposed in this paper. The iteration number and calculation time of the proposed algorithm have been compared with different load flow methods such as Newton-Raphson (NR), fast-decoupled (FD) and a bus elimination (BE) method, with respect to different load characteristics and different system R/X ratios. Simulation result shows that the proposed method is as fast as FD and much faster than NR and BE in general. Moreover, a definite advantage over FD is that the convergence of the proposed technique is not affected by the R/X ratio of the system and accurate load characteristics can be modeled.

articleTitle: Mathematical modelling of loads and voltage support devices for power system voltage stability
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: This paper investigates the mathematical modelling of loads and voltage support devices on the dynamic voltage stability of power systems. The analysis focuses on the potential effects of the interactions among loads, excitation system, LTC and SVC on the voltage stability. The results are based on load flow and eigenvalue analysis of the linearized models of power systems.

articleTitle: Modelling, design and simulation of generator excitation systems by using object oriented techniques and improved genetic algorithms
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: A new approach is proposed to use object oriented techniques and improved genetic algorithms in developing software to design, simulate and model an excitation control system. An example is used to illustrate the feasibility of this approach. The excitation control system is modelled by using both a three-phase representation and transfer function approach. The thyristor exciter offers possibilities for improving dynamic/transient performance.

articleTitle: A new environment for improving accuracy of load forecasting using load and weather data
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: The temperature observation point is one of the most important factors for accurate load forecasting of daily peak load. For development of information and communication technology, electric companies utilize additional observation data. In this paper, we analyzed the relationship between forecast accuracy and temperature observation point, using these data.

articleTitle: Modeling for a large scale hydropower station simulator based on the object-oriented facility
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: Because a large-scale hydroelectric power station simulator in the authors' laboratory has a special functional requirement that all simulation be generating sets oriented, generating processes oriented and whole zone station oriented, modeling of a large scale hydropower station has other characteristics in addition to general simulator modeling characteristics. The authors have used an object-oriented methodology in modeling this large-scale hydropower station and have obtained satisfactory results in some degree. The architecture of modeling for this simulator is presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Automatic reactive compensation at 11 kV
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: In order to fulfil reactive power requirements, capacitors need to be switched in during the load pickup period in the morning and switched out during the load dropping period in the evening. This creates a heavy workload on the control engineers, distracting their attention in monitoring the power system and delaying their responses to site operations. In order to reduce the workload of the control engineers, China Light and Power Co. Ltd. studied several methods of automating these switching operations. Finally, it was decided to develop a software application to automate the switching of these capacitors. This paper describes this automatic capacitors switching application.

articleTitle: Advances in Power System Control, Operation & Management
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)

articleTitle: APSCOM-97. Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management (IEE Conf. Publ. No.450)
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)

articleTitle: Object-oriented optical interconnection distributed parallel processor array network for integrated substation automation system
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: In order to advance the level of integrated substation automaton system (ISAS), a novel object-oriented optical interconnection distributed parallel processor array network used to ISAS is established. The function unit (FU) and the optical interconnection network (OIN) are important parts of the ISAS. The FUs include protection unit, control unit, monitoring unit, man-machine unit and so on. The massively optical interconnection distributed parallel processor array network consists of various kinds of protection units, control units and other units by means of the OIN. In this paper, the architecture and implementation of FU and OIN are described in detail. Results show that the ISAS not only has high parallel processing ability to coordinate the relationship organically between the FUs, but also has advantages of high speed, large bandwidth, immunity to electromagnetic interference as well as being simple, reliable, economic and easy to compact.

articleTitle: A harmonic consideration for the implementation of light rail transit system in Kuala Lumpur
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: The increasing harmonic pollution appearing in distribution networks due to light rail transit implementation is presented in this paper. A complete analysis is done by using the proposed harmonic power flow analysis program that is able to treat multiple harmonic sources simultaneously, including measurement results and/or theoretical values. The program is based on the direct solution of the admittance matrix. A manual analysis is first developed as a guide before conducting the computation by computer, and as a guide to determining the component modeling-especially the transformer's model. Filter installation looks to be the unique solution in reducing the harmonic level even though it will be costly to the system.

articleTitle: Influences on developments in power system operation
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: The changing nature of the electricity supply industry is introducing many new subjects into power system operation related to trading in a deregulated, competitive market. Commercial pressures on obtaining greater returns from existing assets suggest an increasingly important role for dynamic network management using FACTS devices and energy storage as an important resource in generation, transmission, distribution and customer service. Constraints imposed by environmental considerations include the use of more renewable energy and the possible use of gas via methanol.

articleTitle: Change management [ScottishPower]
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: ScottishPower is one of Scotland's largest industrial companies, employing around 14400 people and reporting an annual turnover of almost #3 billion. The Company was formed in 1990 from the previously nationalised South of Scotland Electricity Board, and was one of only two vertically integrated electricity companies, generating, transmitting, distributing and supplying electricity in the UK. At that time, it served 1.8 million electricity customers in the south of Scotland. Today, the Company has diversified into other utility markets such as water, and waste water services, gas and telecommunications, and now serves 1 in 5 of all UK homes with one or more ScottishPower Services, across 3 varied and important geographical areas. This paper seeks to show how the management of business change has played a key role in the growth of the Company, and to indicate the role played by both internal and external benchmarking in establishing and realising the vision of the shape of the Company.

articleTitle: Fault-tolerance analysis of neural network for high voltage transmission line fault diagnosis
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: On the basis of theoretical analysis and testing of the fault-tolerance property for two kinds of associative memory (AM) neural networks (NN) (multiple-layered feedforward NN-FNN and feedback Hopfield NN), this paper proposes to adopt the Hopfield NN with high fault-tolerance property to solve the problem of transmission line fault diagnosis. It builds an AM NN model structure to realize transmission line fault diagnosis, presents a generalized converse learning algorithm by improving a projection based fake converse learning algorithm and the principle of dividing original samples into modules, and jointly uses them to train NN; thus original samples can be fully memorized, so that the NN's storage capacity and fault-tolerance ability can be increased greatly. Results show that Hopfield AM NN possesses high fault-tolerance ability for disturbed real-time input information sequences, and its fault-tolerance property is obviously better than FNN's, this also sufficiently demonstrates the practical application superiority of Hopfield AM NN in power system fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Integrated scheduling and power application functions for Hong Kong Electric Company's new EMS project
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: To meet the increasing demand for a good quality and economical electricity supply, speedy analysis of large amounts of real-time data of power systems and the development of new strategies for forward looking operation and planning are necessary. These major objectives require high performance in scheduling and power application functions. Hong Kong Electric's (HEC) existing EMS and DMS have been used for more than 10 years. A new EMS/DMS supplied by Siemens are expected to be commissioned in late 1997. The new EMS project takes an integrated approach in linking all the above real time control and studying functions with the use of a common database. This paper describes the expected improvement on day to day operation and planning on these areas with reference to current practices and utilization of available tools in HEC from the user's point of view.

articleTitle: Recent trends in power research: the worldwide and Asia scene
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: Economic expansion and population growth in Asia have caused sharp increases in electricity consumption. Though technology may be essentially "universal", there are regional and cultural factors to be dealt with. As Asia will continue to develop from now on, the technology necessary for and suitable to Asia will be an important part of the technology system of the world. Here, the author argues that, in order to achieve further development in allowing Asia to solve its own problems, the broad activity of R&D should be carried out by electric power supply industries and R&D organizations in this area. International exchange of information and cooperation will increase its efficiency and quality.

articleTitle: An improved regularization method for voltage stability analysis
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical analysis that validates the regularization method proposed by Kataoka (1991) for identifying the power system voltage instability limit. The theory provides a clear and intuitive explanation of how the regularization method works, its limitation and how to handle the limitation. The theory offers constructive guidance for improving the algorithms in the selection of the regularization function and step-length. The improved regularization method is illustrated via numerical examples.

articleTitle: The digital electro-hydraulic control technology for utility steam turbines-DEH-IIIA
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: With the increase of steam turbine unit capacity, the upgrading of the operation steam condition and the operation requirement of the grid on the unit, there has been a much higher requirement on the automation level of the steam turbine. In order to satisfy the operation requirement of large units, it is necessary to expand the controllability of the turbine control system to improve the flexibility, adaptability and dynamic response. Here, the authors describe the development of the DEH-IIIA digital electrohydraulic control technology for electric utility steam turbine applications.

articleTitle: Numerical location of unknown single line-to-ground faults on a 70 KV subtransmission system
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: This paper presents a work to locate, numerically, the unknown single line-to-ground faults on an existing 70 KV subtransmission system. First the paper describes a method to determine the location of the faults by using SIMPOW, a power system simulation software developed by ABB Power Systems AB, Sweden. Based on the models of components in the network analyzed, a model for the whole system is constructed. The simulation is then performed with a three-step approach so that the amount of computational work is dramatically reduced. The results from each step are presented in the paper. It is concluded that the proposed method is an efficient and reasonable approach to locate unknown transient faults on a large system when reliable data of the network are available.

articleTitle: Current situation of China's thermal power generation equipment and its development perspective
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: In this paper, the current manufacturing situation of China's thermal power generation equipment industry is described. The evolution of this industry in the past 50 years, including its development and manufacture, is also involved. Facing the the high-speed development trend of China's power construction work as stipulated in the 9th Five-Year Plan and the Development Outline of Long & Medium Term Target by the year 2010, the development strategy and some practical measurements are proposed.

articleTitle: Economic impact on a conventional utility of non-utility generation producing energy from a non-conventional source
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: When a utility buys electric energy from a nonutility generator (NUG) at short notice, such as a few hours, one of the difficult issues encountered by the utility is the evaluation of the rate (buyback rate) it should pay the NUG such that the utility maximizes its economic benefit. This problem is magnified when NUG produces energy from nonconventional source, wind. Short term buyback rates should be based on the operating cost that a utility avoids by utilizing energy from a NUG. This cost is termed as the avoided operating cost (AOC) in this paper. A comprehensive technique for a thermal power utility is developed to assess the short term AOC. The IEEE-RTS is considered to be a thermal utility in this paper, which is utilized to demonstrate the technique. Some sensitivity studies have been performed and selected results are discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: China's power grid and its development
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: In this paper, the author expresses his views with regard to the current situation of China's power grid, the main problems existing, the development plan and a perspective of China's power grid as well as some problems that require priority study at the moment in the field of power grid technology.

articleTitle: Dealing with system voltage stability
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: In spite of conservative transmission line loading limits for operational security, interconnected power systems continue to suffer extensive and costly collapses following severe disturbances which disrupt system voltage stability. An approach has been developed which can minimise the danger of system voltage instability and at the same time allow much heavier transmission line loadings. The proposal is based on the development of automatic measures which can respond to the effects of unpredictable multiple contingencies which presently would disrupt the transmission grid and lead to collapse. The foundation of this proposal hinges on the initial slow phase, sometimes lasting minutes, that has been described in reported incidents of collapse. This temporary stability shows that initially the power system has a large margin of reactive reserves which abruptly vanishes in the disruptive second phase. By having adaptive automatic responses during the first phase, it becomes possible to capitalise on these large reactive power reserves in permitting much heavier transmission line loadings. The continuous accessability of higher transmission line loadings would gain large savings under normal conditions and the automatic protection would avoid the multi-million dollar costs incurred by extensive and long duration blackouts of the power system.

articleTitle: Searching protection relay response time extremes using genetic algorithm-software quality by optimization
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: In this work, the authors studying the possibilities of automating the searching and measuring of response time extremes of power system protection relay software using genetic algorithm optimization. The idea is to produce test cases in order to find potentially problematic situations causing processing time extremes in the software of an electric network protection relay. The testing was done using a relay software simulator. In the comparison, the genetic algorithm based method was clearly better than a random test method.

articleTitle: Design of artificial neural networks for on-line static security assessment problems
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: The design of artificial neural networks for static security assessment problems is systematically summarised in this paper. The static security assessment (SSA) problem is formulated as a pattern classification or pattern recognition problem which can be solved by artificial neural networks. Kohonen, backpropagation and counterpropagation networks are used for on-line SSA problems in our research. A feasible feature selection technique is also described to reduce the dimension of the input pattern. The tests results indicated that ANN-based SSA approaches have good performance.

articleTitle: Microprocessor-based fuzzy logic controller for improving voltage stability
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: Power system voltage/reactive power control strategies based on fuzzy control theories for shunt capacitors and under-load tap changer (ULTC) transformers are proposed. A fuzzy logic controller, based on a microprocessor, has also been designed for improving power system voltage stability.

articleTitle: A simple data communication scheme of a modular comprehensive automation system for substations
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: In this paper, the requirements of the internal data communication network of a modular comprehensive automation system for substations are described. Then, some technical difficulties encountered during the hardware and software design of the network are discussed. Finally, a data communication scheme among multiple computers is proposed. The main point of the scheme is using the embedded serial port of the series of MCS-96 single chip microcomputer working at different modes. This scheme is proved practical in use for its successful implementation in several power substations.

articleTitle: Computer simulation on a typical VVVF elevator drive-scalar versus vector
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: Variable voltage variable frequency (VVVF) drive technology has been widely used in the elevator industry since the 1980s. In the early 1990s, the vector controlled VVVF drive was introduced from Japan and it is now very popular due to the excellent riding comfort for passengers as well as the fast response rate during normal operation. A computer simulation of vector and scalar controlled VVVF drive has been carried out on a standard induction machine elevator drive dynamic model under pulse width modulated AC supply and comparison of their performance is made. From the simulation results, the applicability of the vector control principle can be studied so that improvement can be made to enhance such a system.

articleTitle: Consultation, the key towards a constructive policy for demand-side management
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: Demand side management (DSM) or integrated resource planning (IRP) attempts to systematise a simultaneous analysis of supply and demand and to examine their various impacts. This analysis requires the assessment of costs incurred and their impact on different types of customers. This evaluation is arduous as it has to be performed in terms of both demand and supply and may vary in time and according to the region considered. At the same time, costs evaluation is to be performed at three levels: international (international trades), governmental (national or regional) and industrial (by sector or by company). It is therefore crucial to position the issue adequately and identify (i) the level of political or economical responsibilities of the decision makers involved in the analysis, (ii) the beneficiaries of the DSM/IRP measures, (iii) the parties incurring the costs involved and (iv) the modalities following which these costs will be shared.

articleTitle: Integer modelling of spinning reserve requirements in short term scheduling of hydro systems: an application to power trading
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: This paper investigates the consequences for power system operation, if links are installed between Sweden and thermal dominated power systems. The authors have applied a short term planning method to high, medium and low load scenarios. For each scenario, they calculate the consequences for different combinations of extra power exchange and the provision of spinning reserve. For different cases, they compare the operation cost, the possibility of using the links as intended and the number of start-ups of hydro units.

articleTitle: Voltage stability proximity indicator in frequency domain based on the modified Jacobian matrix model
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: In this paper, based on the modified Jacobian matrix model, a power system voltage stability proximity indicator in the frequency domain is presented. This indicator can be used to measure the proximity to voltage instability which is caused by either Hopf bifurcation or saddle node bifurcation. It is different from the voltage stability indices presented previously, which only take into account the occurrence of saddle node bifurcation. The results of two power systems show that the proposed indicator can approach nearly 'linearly' to zero in a wide interval around the system critical point.

articleTitle: On-line stability constraint assessment for large complex power systems
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: Power systems around the world are increasingly subject to stability limits. Variation in operating conditions from scenarios used for off-line studies require the adoption of conservative transmission limits. The result is the operation of less economic generation systems leading to unnecessary constraint costs. From an operational perspective, any on-line methods that could identify the generator contributions for a given stability problem and the generation changes required to operate closer to stability limits would be most valuable. This paper presents new developments, which have been carried out at the University of Bath, UK, in the areas of on-line stability constraint cost management for large complex power systems.

articleTitle: A direct adaptive fuzzy power system stabiliser
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: A fuzzy power system stabiliser (FPSS) is developed using the concept of fuzzy basis functions. The linguistic rules, regarding the dependence of the plant output on the controlling signal, are used to build the initial FPSS. Based on the Lyapunov's direct method, an adaptation rule is developed in order to make the FPSS adaptive to changes in operating conditions of the power system. The FPSS is designed for a cogenerator, and simulation studies are based on a one machine-infinite bus model. Nonlinear simulations reveal that the performance of the adaptive fuzzy power system stabiliser (AFPSS) is better than the performance of a conventional (linear) power system stabiliser (CPSS) and a fixed-parameter FPSS for a wide range of operating conditions.

articleTitle: Protective relay experimental kit
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: This paper presents a static protective relay experimental kit that can be used to build-up various conventional relays such as overcurrent relay, directional relay, distance relay and transformer differential relay. The kit consists of several circuit modules composed of amplifiers and CMOS gate circuits and it has the advantages of low power loss and is small in size. It is a convenient tool for studying protective relays for education purposes.

articleTitle: A new algorithm for distribution feeder expansion planning for urban area
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: In this paper, in order to support the planners' decision for feeder expansion planning, the authors propose a method that the least cost expansion facilities can be obtained by searching all the candidates which satisfy the expansion constraints such as voltage drop as well as geographical installation restrictions. In the proposed method, dual efficient gradient method, Dijkstra method, Ford-Fulkerson method and tabu search are implemented to obtain a superior feeder expansion plan. Through numerical examples, the validity of the proposed method is verified.

articleTitle: Powering towards the millennium
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: As in previous years, APSCOM '97 is concerned with all aspects of electricity supply, covering company structure and management, technical developments, operational experience and a variety of factors stemming from continued requirements for supply growth. In this opening statement, the author briefly overviews a few of the broad range of topics which are covered in much greater detail in subsequent sections of the conference.

articleTitle: A study of fast decoupled load flow for underground cable systems with ill-conditioned branches
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: The ill-conditioned branches of a cable system are of several types since both small reactance and large resistance are known to exist. Furthermore, capacitance of conductors to earth is much larger than that of its overhead line counterpart. As a result, voltage instability accompanied by convergence difficulties may occur. Both series and parallel compensation schemes have been investigated. The approach has been to use an empirical investigation to determine the optimal compensation levels. No successful cases can be reported for the parallel scheme. For the series scheme, the optimal compensation level is voltage class dependent. After compensation, convergence speed is much slower than for the overhead line case. The reasons are discussed.

articleTitle: High impedance fault (HIF) protection of the transmission line
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: Some special problems of power system protection under conditions of high impedance faults are discussed in this paper. The performance of the conventional protection principles under HIF are analyzed and the basic requirements for protection under HIF conditions are introduced. Two new technical schemes to resolve this problem are suggested and the effects of these methods are given.

articleTitle: Field evaluation of integrated protection and control system in HEC 11 kV/0.38 kV distribution substations
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: This paper describes the background of installing 11 kV circuit breakers and unit protection in Hong Kong Electric Co. Ltd.'s (HEC) 11 kV/0.38 kV distribution substations on a trial basis for field evaluation. The design concept on how the protection scheme enhances the electricity supply quality is also explained. Furthermore, the paper presents how numerical technology and integrated protection and control concepts are applied to cope with the operational requirements.

articleTitle: The development of power system and power system technology in China
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: Over the past 5 to 10 years, electric power and power systems in China have been developing rapidly. The total installed generation capacity by the end of 1996 reached 236.5GW with an annual production of 1,080 TWh which is ranked the second in the world. There are 6 inter-provincial power networks and 5 independent provincial networks in operation in the mainland of the country. The Three Gorges hydropower project is now entering a important phase of the construction and a large amount of preparation work has been completed for the construction of the Three Gorges power transmission system. The total 26 sets of generators of the Three Gorges power plant will be completely installed before the year 2010. By the year 2020, the interconnection of the power networks of the whole country will be formed based on the interconnections among the Three Gorges power system and other inter-provincial power networks. With the rapid growth of the power systems, new technologies for HVAC/DC power transmission, power system operation and control have been and will be developed and adopted.

articleTitle: Tuning of digital control system for 350 MW coal-fired unit for improved controllability and pick-up performance
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: Unit 7 nominally rated at 350 MW is one of the coal-fired generating units installed in the Lamma power station of The Hong Kong Electric Company Ltd. (HEC). This is the first unit in HEC to adopt boiler turbine coordinated control mode (CC) whereas all previous units employed boiler following turbine mode (BF). However, Unit 7 is required to meet severe step and ramp pick-up performance and with stringent environmental emission limits. During commissioning, the unit operating under the CC mode encountered many control problems such as excessive pressure and temperature fluctuations and failed to meet the guaranteed load pickup requirements. This paper describes how HEC tackled the control problems to achieve fine controllability with the aid of a digital control system.

articleTitle: XADVANCE: a tool for dynamic analysis and its application
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: This paper describes XADVANCE, a newly developed tool to analyze the short-term and long-term dynamics of power systems including dynamically changeable components. This paper first outlines XADVANCE, then describes the following features: (1) because no iterative algorithm is used to calculate network conditions, there is no mathematical instability; and (2) a universal dynamics simulation module is used in integral calculation with a user interface using a block diagram and a one-line diagram. Consequently, new power system components such as FACTS equipment can be easily modeled. This paper also evaluates the validation of the developed tool based on studies on (1) frequency regulation by water heaters, and (2) stabilization using an adjustable speed machine (ASM). XADVANCE is shown to be effective in analyzing the dynamics of complex power systems including advanced equipment.

articleTitle: An alternative approach to assess the reliability worth of network reinforcements
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: This paper focuses on an alternative approach to the socio-economic analysis of power systems. The approach takes into account that a minimum level of reliability is desired in the Norwegian main grid. This will secure a certain standard of power supply and access to the power market. The approach implies that a strict socio-economic criterion sometimes has to be disregarded.

articleTitle: Intelligent distributed control of power plants
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: An Intelligent Distributed Controls Research Laboratory (IDCRL) was developed for the NSF Combined Research and Curriculum Development project, power plant intelligent distributed control. New graduate courses on: (1) power plant dynamics and control; and (2) power plant intelligent distributed control were developed. The capstone power plant intelligent distributed control course covered advanced subjects and laboratory experiments developed in the research portion of the project including: (1) extensions to achieve real-time performance of large scale power plant simulations using Unix network programming; (2) distributed implementation of advanced controller programming in an architecture of workstations and microprocessor-based controllers; and (3) intelligent controls using fuzzy logic, neural networks and genetic algorithms. Along with the curriculum development update, a summary of significant research activities is presented in order to provide a complete overview of the results of the projects.

articleTitle: Emergency control and restoration of power system under disturbance
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: This paper discusses China Light and Power Company operating criteria and the generation reserve requirements of the interconnected system including Hong Kong Electric Company and Guangdong Electric Power Holding Company. Emergency actions in the areas of generation reserve application, under-frequency load shedding, under-frequency system decoupling scheme, voltage reduction, manual load shedding, controlled load shedding and blackstart are described. The power system simulator is used as a principal tool to train control engineers to take appropriate emergency actions during power system disturbance.

articleTitle: On-line security optimisation of large power systems using artificial intelligence techniques
publicationTitle: 1997 Fourth International Conference on Advances in Power System Control, Operation and Management, APSCOM-97. (Conf. Publ. No. 450)
abstract: This paper presents a method for the robust on-line optimisation of power system transient stability and economy. It is intended that such a tool will be able to continually adapt to on-line changes in demand and availability in a power system and provide advice to power system operators to allow substantial cost savings and reduce the need for additional power system reinforcement. A detailed description of the method, which utilises the power of three different artificial intelligence techniques, is presented. This is accompanied by the results of a series of tests which demonstrate both the overall suitability of the method and clearly show a substantial improvement over traditional optimisation techniques.
